lines.t: Got the coals burnin’ hotter than July,
Uncle Ray’s flippin’ steaks while the kids run by.
Cousin Joe’s tellin’ jokes way too loud,
Grandma’s laughin’ under that picnic shroud.
Me and Bud got tongs like swords in hand,
Talkin’ ‘bout truth while we overcook the turkey ham.
He says, “Brother, did you read that site? —
The Volumes of Truth kept me up all night!”
We’re talkin’ holy smoke and barbecue,
Blessed be the brisket and the chicken too.
If the Lord can make loaves feed a crowd or two,
He can turn my burnt ends into something new.
So pass that sauce, let’s testify,
Spirits high and the meat ain’t dry.
Yeah, we’re breakin’ bread the backyard way —
Grace and charcoal, that’s how we pray.
Neighbor Jim showed up with a smile so wide,
Said, “Heard y’all preachin’ ‘bout the Lord outside.”
We said, “Pull up a plate, grab a corn on the cob,
There’s gospel in the grill if you do your job.”
Bud said, “Man, those letters hit deep,
About love and truth and the faith we keep.”
I said, “Ain’t no pulpit, but I swear it’s true —
We’re grillin’ like prophets with a backyard view.”
We’re talkin’ holy smoke and barbecue,
Blessed be the brisket and the chicken too.
If the Lord can make loaves feed a crowd or two,
He can turn my burnt ends into something new.
So pass that sauce, let’s testify,
Spirits high and the meat ain’t dry.
Yeah, we’re breakin’ bread the backyard way —
Grace and charcoal, that’s how we pray.
Now the sun’s slidin’ low, sky’s pink and sweet,
We’re full of joy and too much meat.
Bud wipes sauce off his face and grins,
Says, “Truth tastes better when the light sets in.”
Holy smoke and barbecue,
The Volumes of Truth and a good lemonade too.
If laughter’s holy and love shines through,
Then heaven’s got a picnic with a better view.
Yeah, grace and laughter light our way —
God’s work well done today.
